introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2019. Duration: Two and a Half (2 1/2) hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

Answer FOUR questions choosing ONE from each section.

Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Layout of the paper: Section A, Map Work (question 1, the only question of its section); Section B, Physical Geography (questions 2 and 3); Section C, Human Geography (questions 4 and 5); Section D, Cameroon Geography (questions 6 and 7).

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées sans source consultable. Les exemples cités sont des exemples reconnus ; aucune statistique précise n'est avancée. Les faits cités (lieux du Cameroun, projets hydroélectriques, exemples mondiaux) sont à faire relire par un géographe avant toute mise en avant.

Carte non fournie : la question 6(a)(i) s'appuie sur la carte du Cameroun remise le jour de l'épreuve (absente du PDF) ; l'énoncé porte « [outline map of Cameroon supplied on the day, not reproduced here] » et le corrigé donne les noms et la position des éléments à placer.

Question 6(a)(i) : les « watersheds » sont lus comme des lignes de partage des eaux ; le Plateau de l'Adamaoua et les Hautes Terres de l'Ouest (Bamenda) sont des réponses usuelles de manuel, à faire relire par un géographe.
Question 6(c) : les mesures citées sont générales (goudronnage, entretien, Fonds Routier, ponts, pont-bascule) ; aucun projet nommé ni chiffre n'est avancé.
Points : 5 + 3 = 8 ; 4 ; 4 ; 4 ; soit 20 pour la question, conformes au sujet.

questions.enonce_markdown:
6. (a) (i) Using the Cameroon map provided, **locate** and **name** the following:

- Two tourist attractions
- Two watersheds;
- One major town.

(5 marks)

(ii) Suggest THREE measures that may be taken by the government to reduce rural exodus.

(3 marks)

[outline map of Cameroon supplied on the day, not reproduced here]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Locating and naming on the map.** Each feature is marked on the outline map of Cameroon with a dot (or a shaded area for a highland) and its name written beside it. Examples with their positions:

- **Tourist attractions**: **Mount Cameroon** (an active volcano in the South West Region, near Buea and Limbe, on the coast of the Gulf of Guinea); **Waza National Park** (the Far North Region, near the border with Chad). (Others: the beaches of Limbe and Kribi, the Lobe Falls at Kribi, the Sultan's palace at Foumban.)
- **Watersheds** (high ground that separates the rivers flowing to different basins): the **Adamawa Plateau** (central Cameroon, around Ngaoundere) and the **Western (Bamenda) Highlands** (the West and North West Regions). (The Mandara Mountains in the Far North can also be given.)
- **One major town**: **Douala** (the Littoral Region, at the Wouri estuary, the chief port and the economic capital). (Or Yaounde, the political capital, in the Centre Region.)

Marks are given for the correct name and the correct position of each feature, and for the neatness of the map.

**(ii) Three measures to reduce rural exodus**

1. **Provide social amenities and infrastructure in villages**: schools, health centres, electricity, drinking water and good feeder roads, so that rural life is more attractive.
2. **Develop agriculture and rural jobs**: give farmers credit, inputs, training and markets, set up agro-processing and small industries in rural areas, and ensure fair prices for farm products.
3. **Spread development and employment to other regions** (decentralization): locate industries, administration and universities in different regions, so that fewer people leave for Douala and Yaounde.

One mark for each measure.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) State FOUR factors responsible for the urban growth of the coastal belt.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The coastal belt of Cameroon (Douala, Limbe and Kribi) has grown quickly because of:

1. **Ports and trade**: the sea ports (above all Douala) handle imports and exports, and bring commerce, jobs and many people.
2. **Industries**: many factories and agro-industries (processing, a refinery at Limbe, breweries and others) offer jobs.
3. **Plantations and a good agricultural region**: the fertile volcanic and forest land supports large plantations (banana, rubber, oil palm) and their processing.
4. **Rural-urban migration and natural increase**: people move to the coast looking for work, schools and hospitals, and the births in the towns add to it.
5. **Good transport and services**: road, rail and air links and banks, schools and health services attract more settlers.

(Any four; one mark for each.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Describe the ways that the government is using to improve on road transport in Cameroon.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Construction and tarring of roads**: the government builds new tarred roads and tars earth roads, particularly the main roads linking the regional capitals and the ports, and roads to neighbouring countries.
2. **Rehabilitation and regular maintenance**: damaged roads are repaired and maintained, with money from the national budget and from the Road Fund (Fonds Routier) financed by road-user levies.
3. **Bridges and rural roads**: bridges are built over rivers, and feeder roads are opened or repaired to bring farm produce from the villages to the markets.
4. **Control and road safety**: weighbridges to control the loads of heavy trucks, road signs, traffic police and the control of vehicles' roadworthiness; and partnerships with foreign donors and private companies for large projects.

One mark for each way described.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) Name TWO drainage basins and TWO rivers that drain into them.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cameroon is drained by four main basins. Two of them, with two rivers each:

1. **The Atlantic (Gulf of Guinea) basin**: the **Sanaga** and the **Wouri** (also the Nyong, the Ntem, the Mungo and the Cross River).
2. **The Lake Chad basin**: the **Logone** and the **Chari**.

(Other valid basins: the Niger basin, drained by the Benue and its tributary the Faro; the Congo basin, drained by the Dja and the Sangha.) One mark for each basin and one for each correct river.
